items.caseName: Babita Chopra v. State (GNCT of Delhi)
items.coram: Justice J.B. Pardiwala, Justice K. Vinod Chandran
items.headline: Proof that a document was actually executed outweighs a handwriting expert's opinion, says Supreme Court
items.text: The Court held that direct evidence proving a document was executed can outweigh a handwriting expert's opinion when deciding whether the document and signature are genuine, because opinion evidence cannot override substantive proof. Expert opinions are not to be viewed with suspicion, but how much weight they carry depends on the facts. The appeal was allowed, the criminal proceedings were found unsustainable, and the probate proceedings are to be decided quickly.
items.why: Clarifies how courts should weigh handwriting-expert reports against direct proof in forgery and will disputes.

items.caseName: Chander Pal v. Rahul @ Vikram
items.coram: Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra, Justice Shree Chandrashekhar
items.headline: Delay in trial is no ground for bail when the accused has a criminal record and a prior conviction
items.text: The Supreme Court set aside a Punjab & Haryana High Court order granting bail to a murder accused, because his earlier conviction for attempting to murder the same victim had been hidden from the High Court. The right to a speedy trial does not support bail obtained through incorrect statements. The bail was cancelled and the accused was told to surrender.
items.why: Signals that concealing criminal antecedents can undo bail even where the trial has been long delayed.

items.caseName: Kerala Police Officers Association v. State of Kerala
items.coram: Justice B.V. Nagarathna, Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva
items.headline: Supreme Court stays Kerala High Court ruling that allowed abolition of the Kerala Police Officers' Association
items.text: The Court stayed a Kerala High Court Division Bench judgment of 12 November 2026. That judgment had upheld the State's 27 July 2026 order restructuring the recognised police associations, which abolished the KPOA and split its members between two other associations. A Single Judge had earlier quashed the order, finding it inconsistent with the associations' bylaws and passed without a hearing.
items.why: Keeps the KPOA alive while the challenge to the State's restructuring of police associations is heard.

items.caseName: P. Sethuraj v. Union of India
items.coram: CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V. Mohana
items.headline: Son who joined Russian Army: Supreme Court asks Centre to consider humanitarian intervention
items.text: A father asked the Court to bring back his son, who went to Russia on a student visa, reportedly took Russian citizenship and joined the Russian Army. The bench noted that India can do only so much if he has given up Indian citizenship, but asked the Solicitor General to take instructions on humanitarian intervention. The matter is listed in January 2027.

items.caseName: Shri Bhagwan Shrikrishna Lala Virajman and 4 Others v. U.P. Sunni Central Waqf Board 3A and 3 Others
items.headline: Citing a fake judgment is misconduct, but does not undo a sound order
items.text: The Court dismissed a plea to recall its earlier order on who may act as the deity's next friend in the Mathura-related suit. The plaintiffs said the order relied on two fabricated Supreme Court rulings, but the Court found it rested on the Order XXXII CPC rules, not on those cases. It said citing fabricated judgments may be professional misconduct but does not invalidate a decision based on sound law.
items.why: Fake or AI-generated citations are a growing problem in Indian courts.

items.caseName: Praveen Sonkar v. State of U.P. and Another
items.coram: Justice Alok Mathur and Justice Amitabh Kumar Rai
items.headline: Pending inquiry does not stop compulsory retirement of a judicial officer
items.text: The Lucknow Bench upheld the compulsory retirement of a former Additional District and Sessions Judge. It held that such an order is not a punishment and rests on the officer's overall service record, so pending departmental inquiries on the same complaints do not make it invalid. The writ petition was dismissed.

items.caseName: Ashok Kumar Agarwal v. The UCO Bank Ltd. and 3 Others
items.headline: Employee need not prove harm from documents the bank withheld
items.text: The Court held that an employee facing a departmental inquiry cannot be made to prove prejudice from documents the employer kept back. It quashed a UCO Bank employee's dismissal, the appellate order and a recovery of Rs 1,44,616, citing withheld documents, a one-witness inquiry and a cryptic appeal order. The bank must refund any recovered amount and decide his dues within three months.

items.caseName: Blink Digital India Private Limited v. Facebook India Online Services Private Limited and Another
items.headline: Meta is a private company; Court refuses to order account restoration
items.text: The Court declined an interim order directing Meta to restore Blink Digital's business pages and Instagram account. It said Meta is a private entity whose duties to users are contractual, and found no strong prima facie case for a mandatory injunction. Blink Digital may seek restoration by undertaking to follow Meta's policies, and Meta must decide within two weeks and preserve the data.

items.caseName: Court on Its Own Motion v. State Govt. of NCT of Delhi & Anr.
items.coram: Justice Navin Chawla and Justice Arun Bhardwaj
items.headline: JJ Act cases must move to Children's Courts, even pending ones
items.text: Answering a reference from a sessions judge, the Division Bench held that Section 86(4) of the Juvenile Justice Act, added by the 2021 amendment, applies retrospectively. Pending JJ Act trials before magistrates must be transferred to Children's Courts. General IPC or BNS offences against a minor are not exclusively triable by a Children's Court unless another law says so.
items.why: Affects where every pending JJ Act trial in Delhi is heard.

items.caseName: Dhiren Chassa & Anr. v. Mukut Dutta & Ors.
items.headline: Old lawyer's negligence can justify excusing delay in restoring a suit
items.text: The Court upheld a Charaideo civil judge's order excusing a 148-day delay in seeking restoration of a suit dismissed for default, which the plaintiffs blamed on their earlier counsel. It distinguished a Supreme Court ruling that involved a much longer delay and suppression of facts. It also said a revision under Section 115 CPC, not Article 227, was the proper remedy.

items.caseName: Zeeshan Shafi v. UT of J&K
items.headline: PSA detention of man acquitted in UAPA case quashed; release ordered
items.text: The Court quashed the Public Safety Act detention of Zeeshan Shafi Sheikh, finding police kept judging him by a UAPA case in which he had been acquitted. The District Magistrate had adopted the SSP Anantnag's dossier without applying his own mind. The detention and its approval, confirmation and extension orders were set aside and his immediate release from Kot Bhalwal jail was ordered.

items.caseName: Ashok Kumar Gandotra & Ors. v. Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir
items.headline: Giving contract without fresh tender can be criminal misconduct
items.text: The Court refused to quash a corruption charge sheet and charges against former Jammu Development Authority officials and a contractor. They allegedly cancelled a tender where another firm was lowest and then gave the work to the contractor without fresh tenders. The Court said this prima facie showed abuse of official position, and the loss dispute must be decided at trial.

items.caseName: Mohd. Zafer v. State of J&K and Others
items.headline: Complainant's affidavit cannot sink rape charge sheet after S.164-A statement
items.text: The Court refused to quash a rape charge sheet under Section 376 RPC. It held that once the victim's statement under Section 164-A CrPC is recorded, an affidavit by the complainant sworn during investigation is no ground to quash. A medical report that does not support the prosecution is also not enough, and interim directions were vacated.

items.caseName: UT of J&K v. Dev Raj
items.coram: Justice Sanjeev Kumar and Justice M.A. Chowdhary
items.headline: In-charge start no reason to deny promotion arrears
items.text: The Division Bench upheld a tribunal order regularising a PWD employee's promotion as Section Officer from when he was placed in charge or became eligible, whichever is later. It found he met the Recruitment Rules' service requirement when placed in charge. Arrears could not be denied just because the post was first held on an in-charge basis.

items.caseName: Pawan Kumar Mandal v. State of Jharkhand
items.headline: Senior IAS officer can't be kept as Joint Secretary over unfiled property return
items.text: The Court held that failure to file an annual property return is no ground to deny an IAS officer a posting matching his seniority unless a rule allows it. Keeping him as Joint Secretary while 2015-batch officers served as Additional Secretaries was arbitrary. The State must post him as Additional Secretary or an equivalent post within six weeks.

items.caseName: K.N. Ramesh v. State of Karnataka & Anr.
items.headline: Sringeri ballot tampering case against BJP's DN Jeevaraj quashed
items.text: The Court quashed the criminal case against BJP leader D.N. Jeevaraj and two election officials over alleged postal ballot tampering during the Sringeri recount, mainly because the complaint was filed too late. It rejected the argument that a polling agent cannot complain. Allowing a probe after such delay would be an abuse of process, it said.
items.why: Ends a politically charged case tied to the 2023 Sringeri result.

items.caseName: Rakesh Sanjeeva Shetty v. State of Karnataka & Anr.
items.headline: Magistrate to decide Power TV MD's pleas in Siddaramaiah 'sting' video case
items.text: The Court disposed of the Power TV managing director's petition by directing the magistrate to hear his four applications, listed for 1 December. They seek preservation of seized devices and CCTV footage, protection, a lawyer's presence during questioning and the case diary. The State told the Court the CCTV footage had already been preserved.

items.caseName: Anil Maiya v. State of Karnataka & Anr.
items.headline: 'Chargesheet without head and tail': calf photo case quashed
items.text: The Court quashed a case against a man accused of circulating a photo of a calf without a tail. The photo itself was not part of the charge sheet and the prosecution could point to no other material showing he published it. Putting him through trial was unjustified.

items.caseName: Noor Ali v. Sama Adil
items.headline: Father's wish for a 'better' school not enough to move child
items.text: The Court dismissed a father's plea to shift his nine-year-old son from Deens Academy, Whitefield, to Greenwood High. A parent's belief that another school is better does not justify a change when no shortcoming in the current school is shown. It also weighed the longer commute, the mother working at the present school and the higher fees.

items.caseName: Case title not yet reported
items.headline: Notice to State on Pavithra Gowda's fresh bail plea in Renukaswamy murder
items.text: The Court sought the State's response to a fresh bail plea by Pavithra Gowda, first accused in the Renukaswamy murder case. Her earlier High Court bail was cancelled by the Supreme Court in August 2025 and a sessions court rejected a fresh plea on 26 September. She argues her role should be judged separately and that 34 witnesses have been examined.

items.caseName: R. Premkumar v. State of Kerala and Ors.
items.headline: No pre-arrest bail for ex-BLM Society president in fund misappropriation case
items.text: The Court refused anticipatory bail to the former president of the Bharath Lajhna Multi State Housing Co-operative Society, accused of misappropriating crores. The probe is at an early stage and custodial questioning is needed. An affidavit by the complainant saying the dispute was settled did not help, as the record prima facie showed large-scale misappropriation.

items.caseName: C.K. Usman Haji v. Union of India & Ors.
items.coram: Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji
items.headline: No stay on reconstitution of Kerala Waqf Board
items.text: The Division Bench declined to stay the State's reconstitution of the Kerala State Waqf Board, noting the new board has already taken office and remains subject to the pending writ petitions. It set aside a single judge's direction to refer the petitions to another Division Bench. The registry will list the petitions before the roster bench.

items.caseName: Abdul Rafeek @ Rafeek v. State of Kerala and Ors.
items.headline: Police can't force accused to hand over incriminating phone
items.text: The Court held that Section 94 BNSS cannot be used to make an accused produce a mobile phone or other things that may incriminate him, as this would breach Article 20(3). It still upheld the cancellation of his bail in a POCSO case, finding custodial interrogation necessary. Questioning a person on bail is not the same as custodial interrogation, it said.

items.caseName: Jose A.M. v. District Collector and Others
items.headline: Becoming a nun does not end a Christian woman's inheritance rights
items.text: The Court upheld equal distribution of land acquisition compensation among a petitioner and his siblings. A sister's entry into a religious order did not extinguish her share, and co-owners living away still get solatium. An unregistered family arrangement could not defeat a brother's share.

items.caseName: Yusuf v. State of MP
items.headline: Holding a minor's hand with sexual intent is sexual assault under POCSO
items.text: The Court dismissed an appeal against a conviction under Sections 7 and 8 of the POCSO Act. It held that grabbing a minor girl's hand with sexual intent, as proved here, is sexual assault. The victim's age was proved by official records and her evidence was consistent.

items.caseName: State of MP v. Tapas Basak
items.headline: State gets leave to appeal acquittals in turtle and pangolin smuggling case
items.text: The Court granted the State leave to appeal against the acquittal of several accused in an alleged wildlife smuggling racket involving red-crowned roof turtles and pangolins. The CBI, which took over the probe, was allowed to join as intervenor. The matter will be registered as a criminal appeal and the trial records sent for.

items.caseName: J. Jaaswant v. The District Collector and Ors.
items.coram: Justice G.R. Swaminathan and Justice M.D. Sumathi
items.headline: Obey Supreme Court on Thiruparankundram lamp; calls to defy it barred
items.text: The Madurai Bench told the Madurai Collector and police to carry out the Supreme Court's 20 November order allowing the Karthigai Deepam to be lit on Thiruparankundram hill, saying a pending review is no excuse. It restrained the public from calling for defiance of that order, while allowing criticism. It said the prohibitory order must respect devotees' Article 25 rights and ordered release of those unlawfully detained.
items.why: Reminds State officials that Supreme Court orders bind them under Article 144.

items.caseName: Thrisuli v. The Secretary and Others
items.headline: Media gagged in sexual harassment case against Kallakurichi MLA
items.text: In interim orders, the Court barred the press from publishing details protected by Section 16 of the PoSH Act in the case against TVK MLA Arul Vignesh and ordered related social media posts taken down. It appointed IPS officer Shristi Singh to investigate the FIR and another officer to monitor the probe. The matter returns on 27 November for a progress report.

items.caseName: Ramasubbu v. K. Gopal, IAS and Others
items.coram: Justice G.R. Swaminathan and Justice M.D. Sumathi
items.headline: Contempt notice to former libraries director in book-buying scam case
items.text: The Court issued contempt notice to a former Director of Public Libraries over alleged wilful disobedience of its judgment on library book procurement. It said the State's coming procurement policy must be enforceable and ordered production of procurement files and two decades of library-cess accounts. The matter is posted after four weeks.

items.caseName: Deepak Kumar v. State of Bihar and Ors.
items.caseNo: LPA No. 930 of 2023 in CWJC No. 264 of 2021
items.coram: Justice Rajeev Ranjan Prasad and Justice Ranjan Kumar Jha
items.headline: Writ court can't order fresh look at mutation already rejected
items.text: The Division Bench set aside a single judge's direction to the Sampatchak Circle Officer to decide a mutation application afresh, when the application had already been rejected and that rejection was never challenged. Such a direction effectively overturns the statutory authority's order. The appeal was allowed.

items.caseName: Kanhaiya Singh v. State of Bihar and Others
items.headline: No reconsideration of voluntary retirement once punishment is imposed
items.text: The Court dismissed a medical officer's challenge to his termination. A voluntary retirement request must be weighed with pending disciplinary proceedings, and once those ended in punishment his request could not survive. It found no legal flaw in the termination order.

items.caseName: Dr. Botcha Anusha v. The State of Telangana and 4 Others
items.headline: Police to have defamatory posts on YSRCP leader taken down
items.text: The Court directed the Cyber Crime police SHO to have YouTube and Meta remove derogatory posts about YSRCP leader Botcha Anusha, after verification, whenever she complains. The direction covers future complaints too. Police said 31 of 33 flagged posts were already deleted.

items.caseName: Kodicherla Mahendar v. State of Telangana & Anr.
items.headline: FIR over burning 'Cockroach Janata Party' banner quashed
items.text: The Court quashed proceedings against a former BJP corporator accused of trying to burn a banner at a Ravana Dahan event and obstructing officials. The complaint described no assault or criminal force. Mere obstruction or a verbal row does not make out the offence, it held.

items.caseName: Bittu Mistri v. State of Uttarakhand
items.headline: Police can't harass a citizen at midnight without an FIR
items.text: The Court said police get the power to investigate only after an FIR for a cognizable offence is registered. It restrained police from harassing the petitioner or visiting his home without legal authority, after he alleged a midnight visit and a Rs 40 lakh demand. It ordered protection for him within 24 hours.
